findings.classification: core module defect: shared-cost/batch parent ownership
findings.title: Batch child trusts a parent-row label without proving an actual charged parent attempt
findings.evidence: Validation checks processing status, owner, lease, scope, and charge_attempt_id equality, but does not verify a charged shared-quota ledger entry or another authoritative parent charge receipt. The batch path then sets allowed=True and skips charge. The existing test deliberately seeds only photo_ingredient_batch_quota_ops; it asserts quota remains 3 and even that no text_meal_estimate_quota_ledger table exists, while the provider is called successfully.
findings.minimal_repro_prediction: Use the existing runtime with quota=3; insert exactly the synthetic processing batch row used by test_photo_child_uses_parent_charge_attempt_and_does_not_spend_again, without calling the parent shared-charge primitive; invoke create_text_meal_estimate_draft with its batch key/owner. Predicted: provider call succeeds, draft is pending, quota remains 3, and no authoritative charged ledger row exists.
findings.required_contract: Bind and verify an authoritative parent charge/claim receipt transactionally; equality of two caller-controlled row fields is not proof of ownership/payment.

findings.title: Expired pre-provider claimed attempts are irreversibly treated as provider-started unknown
findings.evidence: On any expired estimating lease, recovery changes the draft to provider_unknown and changes both attempt states claimed and provider_started to unknown. It never reads the prior state or provider_started_at and HostDependencies has no refund primitive. Thus the durable provider-start marker is not honored for the safe pre-start crash case.
findings.minimal_repro_prediction: Seed an expired estimating draft, a real charged shared-quota attempt, and text_meal_provider_attempts.state='claimed' with empty provider_started_at; do not call the provider. Redeliver the same message. Predicted: TextMealProviderError result-unknown, attempt becomes unknown, no provider call, quota remains debited, and every later redelivery is permanently blocked.
findings.required_contract: Under the same owned transaction, inspect the attempt state: claimed with no provider-start marker may use the real owned refund primitive and become retryable; provider_started must remain unknown and must never refund or blind-retry.

findings.classification: integration blocker: batch parent fail/refund race
findings.title: Child provider-start is not durably propagated to the batch parent charge owner
findings.evidence: A child records provider_started only in text_meal_provider_attempts under its fresh child attempt_id; quota_attempt_id merely contains the parent owner string. No update or callback marks photo_ingredient_batch_quota_ops or the authoritative parent claim as provider-started. There is also a transaction gap after child claim commit and before child provider-start commit. Targeted parent search confirms a real owned refund primitive exists at shared_ai_quota.py:80-81 and 96-107, but this module does not bind it or a parent batch transition API.
findings.minimal_repro_prediction: Allow a child under a processing parent; after the child transaction at line 595 commits, expire/fail the parent before or just after the child's provider-start transaction, then execute parent refund/reclaim logic. Predicted risk: parent code cannot learn from its own row that a child provider may have started, so it can refund/retry the shared charge while the first provider result is in flight. Exact outcome is BLOCKED pending the unimplemented parent claim/fail/refund binding.
findings.required_contract: Parent claim/fail/refund must share a durable provider-start marker with every child and fail closed: once any child can have crossed provider start, parent failure must not refund or retry. Claim validation and start marking need an atomic/version-fenced parent ownership protocol.

findings.title: Completed batch child cannot be replayed after the parent leaves processing
findings.evidence: Batch scope/lease validation executes before lookup of an existing child draft. Therefore replay depends on the parent still being processing with an unexpired lease, even when this exact user/message already has a completed pending draft and needs no provider or charge.
findings.minimal_repro_prediction: Run the successful photo-child test once; update its parent batch status to completed (or expire its lease); call the same child message again. Predicted: ValueError batch scope invalid instead of returning the existing draft; provider and quota remain unchanged.
findings.required_contract: Define an authenticated idempotent replay path for an already-owned exact child before requiring a live parent processing lease, while still rejecting changed user/message/request/batch ownership.

coverage_gaps: No test covers expired state='claimed' before provider start and the corresponding owned refund/retry behavior.
No test proves a real parent shared charge exists for a photo batch; the current positive test proves the opposite.
No test drives parent claim/fail/refund against a child provider-start marker.
No test replays a completed child after parent completion or lease expiry.
Reduced test schema is not the actual parent daily-food initializer.
Provider SDK shape is fake; actual SDK/router/LINE entry paths were not exercised.
integration_bindings_missing: owned quota refund primitive for definitely pre-provider attempts
atomic parent-visible provider-start transition or query
parent batch fail/reclaim policy that refuses refund/retry after any possible provider start
actual host schema initializer and migration compatibility proof
actual isolated provider SDK adapter and router entry wiring

conclusion.reason: The single-request post-start unknown fence is conservative, but pre-start lease recovery ignores that marker, batch children can consume provider work without proof of a real parent charge, parent refund/retry cannot observe child provider start, and batch redelivery breaks after parent lifecycle transition. Passing 11 narrow tests does not close these defects.

limitations: Review is fixed to the three recorded hashes and the stated line counts.
Only targeted parent symbol search was used; no complete server.py review and no claim that parent behavior was fully characterized.
IR-003 is an integration blocker/risk prediction, not a demonstrated parent E2E failure, because the required binding is absent and live root import was prohibited.
No broad regression or external side-effect test was run.
